nodes.name: Next-attempt webhook
nodes.notes: Meant to be called right after post-call-synthesis.workflow.json produces a Disposition, to decide what happens to this record next. Input contract: {opportunityId, disposition, attemptCountThisWave, wave (1-4), lastAttemptDate}. ASSUMES the dialer/hopper (W3.1/W3.2, not built - schema depends on the scraper's own output) is the thing that actually tracks attemptCountThisWave and wave and passes them in here; this workflow is pure decision logic, not state storage.

nodes.name: Apply attempt matrix
nodes.notes: The one workflow in this library with real, brief-specified business logic encoded directly (not a placeholder) - the attempt caps and wave count are given numbers, not invented. Still not wired to anything live: nothing in this repo yet tracks attemptCountThisWave/wave/lastAttemptDate as real state (that's the hopper, W3.1/W3.2, not built), so this is correct decision logic waiting on a caller that has real state to hand it.
